General medicine · plasterRelieves pain and inflammation of joints and muscles

plaster (179901CPL)Products with the same general-name code (179901CPL) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

This medicine is used for the analgesia and anti-inflammation (anti-inflammatory action) of degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis (tendon) and tenosynovitis (tendon sheath synovitis), peritendinitis (around the tendon), humeral (upper arm bone) epicondylitis (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and swelling (edema) and pain following trauma (wounds).

At a glance

Category

General medicine · plaster

How it works

Relieves pain and inflammation of joints and muscles

Why this one

Products with the same general-name code (179901CPL) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

How to apply it

After removing the release liner from the medicated surface, attach to the affected area twice a day.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, photosensitivity, aspirin asthma (asthma caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.) as a patient or a person with such experience, hypersensitivity to tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate, or oxybenzone, if you are a pregnant woman of 6 months or more of pregnancy, or a child under 15 years of age.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma, pregnant women, and breast-feeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Since photosensitivity may occur, avoid ultraviolet rays while using this medicine or for up to 2 weeks after use.
  • Do not use on the eyes and mucous membranes, athlete's foot, or ringworm.
  • When used on damaged skin and mucous membranes, or areas of eczema or rash, it may cause temporary irritation and sharp pain.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing technique.

Possible side effects

  • In rare cases, shock (hypersensitivity-like symptoms such as urticaria, dyspnea, facial swelling, etc.), asthma attack (dry rales, wheezing, dyspnea), and occasionally contact dermatitis such as redness, rash, itching, blisters, erosion, irritation, and swelling, dry skin and pigmentation, photosensitivity due to direct sunlight, and skin rash spreading to the whole body may occur; if so, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

cream (363700CCM)Products with the same general-name code (363700CCM) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

This medicine is used for secondarily infected allergic or inflammatory skin diseases (eczema, contact dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, atopic dermatitis, photodermatitis, chronic simple lichen, intertrigo (skin chafing), exfoliative dermatitis, itching, psoriasis (dry scale disease)), and first-degree burns.

At a glance

Category

General medicine · cream

How it works

Treats infected inflammatory and allergic skin conditions

Why this one

Products with the same general-name code (363700CCM) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased area) 1 to 3 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to this medicine, a person with hypersensitivity to or experience with aminoglycoside antibiotics such as streptomycin, kanamycin, gentamicin, neomycin, etc. or bacitracin, a patient with skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, herpes zoster (blisters), herpes simplex (blisters), chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice), otitis externa (external auditory canal) with eczema accompanied by tympanic membrane perforation, an ulcer (excluding Behcet's disease), a burn or frostbite of second-degree deep type or above (not exposed), perioral dermatitis, common acne, or rosacea (strawberry nose).
  • Before using this medicine, patients or persons with experience of hypersensitivity to propylene glycol, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breast-feeding women, and infants and young children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Keep the prescribed dosage and administration well.
  • When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not use for ophthalmic (eye) use.
  • Do not use for purposes other than treatment such as after makeup or shaving.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing technique without a doctor's supervision.
  • Do not use for a long period of time.

Possible side effects

  • If contagious impetigo (crusted pus disease), folliculitis, viral infection, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, burning sensation, itching, rash, redness (congested and reddened), flushing, edema, papules, small blisters, dry skin, pustular (pus blister) dermatitis, prickly heat, wound aggravation, bedsores, pustulosis, hypersensitivity, skin discoloration, hypertrichosis (excessive hair), acneiform eruption, hypopigmentation, perioral dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, skin erosion, secondary infection, skin atrophy, striae, or increased intraocular pressure and glaucoma (blurred vision) when used on eyelid skin, etc. occur, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

ointment (229102COM)Products with the same general-name code (229102COM) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

This medicine is used for impetigo, infectious eczematoid dermatitis, acne vulgaris (common acne), folliculitis, boils and furunculosis, suppurative hidradenitis, impetiginous eczema, and secondary infections caused by burns, trauma, sutured wounds, and skin graft wounds, due to staphylococci, streptococci, corynebacterium, and clostridium.

At a glance

Category

General medicine · ointment

How it works

Treats bacterial skin infections and secondary infections

Why this one

Products with the same general-name code (229102COM) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

How to apply it

Clean the affected area and apply an appropriate amount directly to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day, or spread it widely on sterile gauze and attach it. Limit the administration period to about 1 week. Do not apply thickly.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to this medicine, or a patient with an infection caused by non-susceptible bacteria (especially Pseudomonas aeruginosa).
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breast-feeding women, and premature infants and newborns should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Since this medicine has high permeability and absorption, do not use it for a long period of time.
  • Do not use for ophthalmic use.
  • Do not use on the inner face such as the eyes or eyelids.

Possible side effects

  • If sensitized symptoms (itching, redness, swelling, papules, small blisters, etc.), temporary burning sensation, occasionally hypersensitivity reactions such as rash, mild pain and irritation, or pain when applied to patients with severe leg ulcers occur, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

cream (A18500CCM)Products with the same general-name code (A18500CCM) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

This medicine is used for wounds and scars in hypertrophic and keloid, movement-restricting, or cosmetic skin damage after surgery, amputation, burns, and accidents, traumatic contracture, and cicatricial stenosis.

At a glance

Category

General medicine · cream

How it works

Treats scars and skin damage after wounds

Why this one

Products with the same general-name code (A18500CCM) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

How to apply it

Massage lightly several times a day until it fully penetrates the wound area. In the case of a severe wound or an old scar, fix it with a dressing and leave it for one night.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to this medicine or methyl parahydroxybenzoate, a pregnant woman, or a patient with incised or unhealed wounds, or wound areas with oozing on mucous membrane skin.
  • Before using this medicine, breast-feeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Be careful not to expose the wound to solar heat or light rays, and in the case of a freshly formed wound, avoid physical irritation such as extreme cold, ultraviolet rays, or strong massage.
  • When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • Very rarely, local skin irritation may occur.

General medicine · patchRelieves joint and muscle pain and inflammation

patch (214005CPC)Products with the same general-name code (214005CPC) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

This medicine is used for degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), tenosynovitis (tendon sheath inflammation), muscle pain, bone and joint pain, post-traumatic pain, and pain after fracture healing.

At a glance

Category

General medicine · patch

How it works

Relieves joint and muscle pain and inflammation

Why this one

Products with the same general-name code (214005CPC) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

How to apply it

Attach 1 patch to the affected area (diseased area) every 2 days.
However, after bathing or showering or when sweating, 1 patch may be attached per day.
Clean and dry the affected area (diseased area), peel off the release liner from the medicated surface, then firmly attach it to the skin and press well with the palm of your hand. In particular, check that the edges of the patch are well attached.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or piroxicam preparations; patients who have or have experienced aspirin asthma (asthma attacks caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.); children 14 years of age or under; and pregnant women, women who may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have bronchial asthma or are elderly.
  • Do not use on skin with lesions (hemorrhagic skin disease, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds), the eyes, or mucous membrane areas.
  • Do not use the occlusive dressing method.

Possible side effects

  • If, occasionally, local itching, redness, rash, scaling, eczema/dermatitis, contact dermatitis, erythema, or, rarely, photosensitivity appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

cream (102935CCM)Products with the same general-name code (102935CCM) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

This medicine is used for herpes simplex (blister) virus infections (including initial and recurrent genital herpes (blisters) and cold sores (blisters)).

At a glance

Category

General medicine · cream

How it works

Treats herpes simplex virus infections including genital and cold sores

Why this one

Products with the same general-name code (102935CCM) share ingredient, strength and form. Check by ingredient and strength, not by product name.

How to apply it

Apply to the affected area (diseased area) 5 times a day at approximately 4-hour intervals. Treatment should be continued for 5 days, and if not cured after 5 days of use, it may be used for an additional 5 days.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, breastfeeding women, or children.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are an immunodeficiency patient such as AIDS or bone marrow transplant, are pregnant or possibly pregnant, or are a patient with or having experienced hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.
  • Start treatment as early as possible, and in recurrent cases, start when prodromal symptoms or lesions first appear.
  • Strictly follow the prescribed usage and dosage.
  • Do not use this medicine for the purpose of preventing infection of others or recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infections.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or mixing with other medicines.
  • Use this medicine for external use only.
  • Do not use on the cornea or mucous membranes for ophthalmic purposes.
  • To prevent this medicine from spreading to other parts of the body or infecting others, apply while wearing a finger cot or rubber gloves.

Possible side effects

  • Discomfort such as tenderness, temporary burning sensation, mild pain including stinging pain, and contact dermatitis, erythematous rash, eczema, allergic reactions, and occasionally irritation at the applied area, itching, vulvitis, facial edema, skin discoloration, hives, rash, vesicular rash, and skin peeling may occur.

Interactions

  • Patients who have been administered probenecid should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
